jess-peopleops: Quick benefits Q  - Can the companys employer match be contributed as Roth (after-tax) into the 401(k), or does our plan only allow pre-tax employer contributions? Trying to advise someone considering in-plan Roth conversions.
ryan-eng: I thought matches are always pre-tax employer dollars and you cant make the match Roth on the employer side. But you can do in-plan Roth conversions of your own pre-tax deferrals in some plans.
emma-finance: Short answer: employer match is typically contributed as pre-tax (traditional) plan money per IRS rules; however some plans permit "designated Roth contributions" for employee deferrals. Whether the plan allows in-plan Roth conversions of employer contributions to Roth is vendor/plan-specific.
jess-peopleops: Okay, so if an employee wants their matched dollars to be Roth, can we convert them later?
emma-finance: Two paths: (1) In-plan Roth conversion: some recordkeepers allow converting pre-tax employer contributions to Roth in-plan, but plan document must authorize it and conversions may be taxable when executed. (2) Rollover to an IRA Roth (post-termination) is another route but again tax applies. I'll check our plan doc and vendor support.
benefits@redwood: Confirming via plan admin: our current recordkeeper supports in-plan Roth conversions for employee pre-tax deferrals but does NOT permit converting employer matching contributions to designated Roth while still employed. Employer contributions can be rolled to a Roth IRA after termination if the employee elects, subject to tax consequences.
ryan-eng: Good to know. So matched money can't be Roth while employed. That means any tax on converting match would happen only after you separate and roll to Roth IRA?
emma-finance: Correct per vendor: converting employer match to Roth IRA post-termination is allowed if plan distribution rules permit an in-service distribution/termination distribution. If employee does an in-plan conversion (where allowed), taxable income is recognized in the year of conversion. For post-termination Roth rollover, taxable treatment depends on whether funds are pre-tax or after-tax in the plan at distribution. We'll put a short explainer in benefits portal.
jess-peopleops: Are there any immediate action items for employees who want Roth treatment for future contributions?
emma-finance: Actions: 1) Employee can elect designated Roth deferrals for future paychecks (if they want Roth treatment on their contributions). 2) Employer match will remain pre-tax unless plan changes. 3) If employee wants match to end up Roth eventually, they should consult tax advisor about post-termination rollover vs potential in-plan conversion (if policy changes). 4) We'll update the FAQ with examples showing tax timing.
payroll-bot: FYI: to start designated Roth deferrals, submit the pre-tax vs Roth contribution election via payroll portal: https://payroll.redwood.com/benefits/contributions :money_with_wings: 
benefits@redwood: We'll follow up with the recordkeeper to confirm whether any future plan amendment could allow employer-designated Roth matches and what governance steps would be required. Case# RK-2026-3344 opened. Will post vendor reply here.
